raw_text:
Here’s the complete 12-week plan summary for your beginner client training in a small flat with a pull-up bar and mat, including strength (with intensified Phase 2), cardio, Saturday finisher options, nutrition, and mobility. Use three strength days/week (e.g., Mon–Wed–Fri), cardio 2–3x/week, Saturday finisher, and at least one full rest day (Sun).

Structure at a glance
- Strength: 3x/week, 35–55 min. Phases: Foundation (Weeks 1–4), Intensified Strength (Weeks 5–8), Strength Density & Pull-up Chase (Weeks 9–12).
- Cardio: 2–3x/week, 15–30 min, low-impact options.
- Saturday finisher: 20–30 min fun session (choose one of 3 formats).
- Mobility: Daily micro (5–8 min), 10-min pre-lift warm-up, 1–2 deep sessions/week.
- Nutrition: Maintenance to slight surplus, high-protein, carbs around training.
- Equipment: Pull-up bar, mat; optional chair/sofa/table; backpack for load.

Phase 1 — Foundation and Movement Quality (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: Learn movement patterns; build tolerance; start pull-up pathway; accumulate volume without soreness. RPE 7–8, 3-1-1 tempo on primaries early.

Weekly format: 3 full-body days (A/B rotate). Warm-up 10 min; rests 60–120s main, 30–60s accessory.

Week 1
- Day A
  - Incline push-up 4x6–8 (controlled)
  - Assisted pull-up 5x3–5 (3–4s eccentrics)
  - Sit-to-stand → air squat 4x8 (3s down + 1s pause)
  - Hip bridge 3x10–12 (2s squeeze)
  - Front plank 3x20–30s
  - Scapular pull-ups 2x8
- Day B
  - Push-up (flat or incline) 4x5–8
  - Inverted row 4x6–8
  - Split squat 3x6–8/leg (3s down)
  - Hinge drill 3x10 + reverse lunge 2x6/leg
  - Side plank 3x20s/side
  - Dead bug 3x6/side

Week 2
- Add 1–2 reps/set where possible; +1 set to primary push/pull; core holds +5–10s. Same exercises/tempos.

Week 3
- Progress leverage:
  - Push-ups: lower incline or light feet-elevated if strong.
  - Pulls: add 1–2 eccentric-only reps after each set.
  - Squats: full air squats with 1s pause if ready.
  - Bridges: single-leg bridge 3x8/leg.
- Keep 4–5 sets push/pull, 3–4 sets legs.

Week 4 (Consolidate/mini-test)
- Push-ups: 3 sets to 1–2 reps in reserve; log best.
- Pulls: 6–8 x 3 assisted (clusters), finish 1–2 sets inverted rows 8–10.
- Squat: 4x8–10 tempo air squats + Bulgarian split squat 2x6–8/leg.
- Bridge: feet-elevated 3x10–12.
- Core: Hollow hold 4x20–30s.

Phase 2 — Intensified Strength Block (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: Push intensity; drive pull-up strength; progress unilateral leg strength. RPE 8–9 primaries; 90–150s rest.

Week 5
- Day A (Heavy push/pull)
  - Push-up (hardest leverage allowing 4–6) 6x4–6, 2–3s down, 1s pause
  - Assisted chin-up 7x3 (5s eccentric last rep/set)
  - Bulgarian split squat 5x5/leg (pause 2s bottom)
  - Hip thrust 4x6–8 (2s squeeze)
  - Hollow hold/rocks 4x25–35s
- Day B (Leg density + pull skill)
  - Tempo backpack front squat or air squat 4x8 at 3–1–X
  - Chin-up EMOM 10 min: 2 assisted reps each minute
  - Pike or decline push-up 5x5–7
  - Single-leg RDL 3x8/leg (3s down)
  - Side plank reach-through 3x25–30s/side
- Day C (Push clusters + pull eccentrics)
  - Push-up clusters: 5 clusters of 6 total reps (e.g., 2+2+2, 20s intra-rest)
  - Chin-up eccentric ladders: 4x(3 reps at 8s/6s/4s lowers)
  - Step-back lunge 4x8/leg
  - Hinge drill + glute bridge 2x15 each
  - Anti-rotation towel press 3x20–25s/side

Week 6 (Leverage up; reduce assistance)
- Day A: Push-up 6x5–6 harder leverage; Chins 8x3 (longer eccentrics on early sets); Bulgarians 5x6/leg; Hip thrust 4x6–8; Hollow rocks 4x12–16.
- Day B: Backpack front squat 5x6–8 (3–1–X); Chin-up EMOM 12 min (alt 2 reps + 1 scap pull); Pike push-ups 5x6–8; Single-leg RDL 4x6–8/leg; Side plank with top-leg raise 3x25–35s/side.
- Day C: Push clusters 6 clusters (add 1 rep total vs Week 5); Chin negatives 5x2 at 8–10s + 1–2 assisted singles; Lunges 4x9–10/leg; Hip thrust pump 3x12; Anti-rotation 3x25–30s/side.

Week 7 (Heaviest week)
- Day A: Push-up 7x3–5 (3s down, 1s pause); Chins 10x2 assisted (least help); Bulgarians 6x4–5/leg; Hip thrust 5x5–6 (2s pause); RKC plank 4x15–20s.
- Day B: Backpack front squat 4x8 (2–0–X, last set AMRAP to 1–2 RIR); Pull-up EMOM 10–12 min (2 reps odd, 1 long eccentric even); Pike push-up deficit 4x5–6; Single-leg RDL 3x8/leg (2s bottom pause); Side plank hip taps 3x12–15/side.
- Day C: Contrast push-ups x5 rounds (4 heavy + 6 speed); Chin ladders 1–2–3 x3 ladders + 1 slow eccentric; Split squat 4x8/leg moderate; Hip bridge iso 2x45–60s + 1x20 pumps; Anti-rotation 3x25–30s/side.

Week 8 (Consolidate/mini-test)
- Day A: Push-up top set to 1–2 RIR at hardest leverage; then 3x4 back-offs (~90% diff). Chins: 6–8 single attempts (or top hold + slow eccentric). Bulgarians 4x6/leg; Hip thrust 3x6–8.
- Day B: Backpack front squat 3x8 easy-moderate; Chin density EMOM 8–10 min (2 reps); Pike push-up 4x6–8; Single-leg RDL 3x8/leg; Core choice 3 sets.
- Day C: Push clusters 4 clusters (16–24 total reps); Chin negatives 3x2 (8–10s) + 2x6–8 inverted rows; Lunge 3x8/leg; Hip bridge pump 2x20; Mobility focus 8–10 min.

Phase 3 — Strength Density & Pull-up Chase (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: Convert strength to higher-quality volume, push toward first strict chin-up, maintain leg strength. 3 full-body days; include EMOMs and clusters.

Week 9
- Day A (Push emphasis, pull skill)
  - Decline or pseudo planche-lean push-up 6x5–8
  - Chin-up clusters 10x1–3 assisted/negatives (30–45s rest; aim 15–25 total reps)
  - Pike push-up 3x6–8
  - Inverted row (feet elevated if strong) 3x8–12
  - Hollow to arch rocks 3x12
- Day B (Lower strength)
  - Bulgarian split squat heavy 5x5/leg (backpack)
  - Backpack front squat/Zercher hold squats 4x8–10 (2–3s down)
  - Hip thrust heavy 4x8–10 (2s pause)
  - Single-leg RDL 3x8/leg
  - Backpack front-hold marches 3x30–45s
- Day C (Pull emphasis, push volume)
  - Pull-up EMOM 10 min: odd 2–3 assisted; even 1 long eccentric (6–8s) + 1 scap pull
  - Push-up volume 5x8–12 at challenging leverage (add backpack if floor is easy)
  - Row variation 3x10–12
  - Core: Side plank reach-through 3x10/side + dead bug 3x8/side

Week 10
- Progress: reduce assistance on chins; attempt 1–2 true bodyweight singles if close. Add slight load to push-ups if >12 reps on floor. Add 10–20% backpack load to Bulgarians or 1 extra set. Optionally extend EMOMs by 2 minutes.

Week 11 (Micro-peak)
- Day A: Chin-up singles practice 8–12 attempts with 60–90s rest—strict reps if possible; otherwise top hold + slow eccentric.
- Day B: Bulgarian split squat 6x4/leg heavy; Hip thrust 5x6–8 heavy; Finish with quad/ham isometrics 2x20–30s.
- Day C: Push-up ladder 1-2-3-4-5-4-3-2-1 (30–40s rests) at chosen leverage; Rows 4x6–8; Chins 3x3–4 light assisted to keep pattern. Core each day (hollow/RKC/anti-rotation).

Week 12 (Deload/test)
- Reduce total sets by 30–40%, avoid failure.
- Tests:
  - Chin-up: 3–4 singles attempts; best outcome = strict rep, long top hold, or 12s eccentric.
  - Push-ups: Max quality set (stop 1 shy of failure).
  - Bulgarians: AMRAP at Week 9–10 load (stop 1–2 RIR).
- Light accessories + mobility focus.

Cardio plan (2–3x/week, 15–30 min)
- Intensity: Mostly RPE 4–6; intervals RPE 7–9 used sparingly.
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): 2x/week
  - Session A steady: 15–20 min low-impact mix (marching, toe taps, shadow boxing) at RPE 4–5.
  - Session B intervals: 8 x 30s hard (RPE 7) + 45s easy; 5-min warm-up, short cool-down.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): 2–3x/week
  - Session C tempo steady: 12–16 min at RPE 5–6 (plus warm-up/cool-down).
  - Session D mixed intervals: 6–10 x 40s hard + 40–60s easy.
  - Session E stairs (if available): 10–15 min continuous stair walks RPE 5–6.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): 2–3x/week
  - Session F ladder intervals: 20–40–60–40–20s x 1–2 ladders with equal rest.
  - Session G longer easy: 15–20 min continuous at RPE 4–5.
  - Session H threshold taste: 3–4 x 3 min at RPE 6–7 with 2 min easy.

Saturday finisher (choose one each week, 20–30 min)
- Option 1 EMOM Gauntlet (20 min): blocks of push-ups + shadow boxing; assisted chins/negatives + climbers; split squats; core + brisk march.
- Option 2 Deck of Cards (15–25 min cap): suits map to push-ups, chins/rows (3–6 reps), split squats (per-leg half card), toe-tap/jacks (seconds = 2x card).
- Option 3 Rings/Bar Playground (if rings added): 4–6 rounds, 45s on/15s off: rows, push-ups, split-squat jumps (or calf-raise), core, shadow boxing. Rest 60–90s between rounds.

Mobility routine
- Daily micro (5–8 min): 90/90 hip lift breaths; cat–cow; thoracic openers; hip CARs; ankle rocks; hip flexor stretch; wrist rocks.
- Pre-lift warm-up (10 min): marching/arm swings; world’s greatest stretch; squat pry; hip airplanes; scapular pulls + shoulder circles; ankle rocks; dead bug + plank.
- Post-session (3–5 min): easy breathing + child’s pose with side reach, doorway pec stretch, hip flexor stretch.
- Deep sessions (15–20 min, 1–2x/week):
  - Session A (hips/ankles/low back): 90/90 switches, pigeon or figure-4, Cossack with support, knee-to-wall ankles, decompression hang.
  - Session B (shoulders/T-spine/wrists): towel-roll T-spine extension, thread-the-needle, doorway pec stretch, lat opener on chair, wall slides, prone Y-T-W, wrist sequence.

Nutrition summary
- Calories: Start at maintenance to slight surplus (+150–250 kcal/day). On training days, bias carbs higher; rest days at maintenance or −0 to −150 kcal if aiming recomposition.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (30–40 g per meal across 3–4 meals).
- Carbs: Pre-workout 30–60 g + protein 20–35 g 60–120 min before; post-workout 25–40 g protein + 40–80 g carbs within 2 hours.
- Fats: 0.7–1.0 g/kg/day, mostly unsaturated.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day; fruits/veg 4–6 servings/day; legumes 3–4x/week.
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day + ~500 ml around training.
- Supplements (optional): Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day; vitamin D3 per local guidance if low sun; omega-3 if not eating fish (consult a professional).
- Weekly habits progression: establish protein and plate method (Weeks 1–2), fiber/consistency (Weeks 3–4), caloric tweaks via weight trends (Weeks 5–6), micronutrients/sleep (Weeks 7–8), performance fueling (Weeks 9–10), keep meals familiar in test week (Weeks 11–12).

Weekly layout example
- Mon: Strength (Phase plan) + pre-lift warm-up + optional 3–5 min cool-down.
- Tue: Cardio (steady or intervals) + Daily micro-mobility + optional Deep Session A.
- Wed: Strength + warm-up.
- Thu: Off or cardio (easy) + Deep Session B mobility.
- Fri: Strength + warm-up.
- Sat: Finisher Day (pick option) + light mobility.
- Sun: Rest, walk, or gentle mobility only.

Progress tracking and targets
- Log sets/reps, leverage/assistance, RPE, and notes.
- Aim by Week 12:
  - 1 strict chin-up (or 12s controlled eccentric and strong assisted doubles).
  - Push-ups: 20+ strict floor reps or 6–10 strong reps at decline/backpack.
  - Bulgarians: solid 5–6 rep sets/leg with front load.
- If two consecutive sessions underperform, reduce volume by ~30% for a week (mini-deload), then resume.

Equipment roadmap (space-friendly)
- Near-term: resistance bands with door anchor; adjustable dumbbells (to ~20 kg/hand) or one heavy kettlebell (16–24 kg); rings/TRX for variety.
- Later: loadable DB handles + small plates, foldable bench, sandbag, dip belt/strap for weighted pull-ups.

Here’s a structured, progressive 12‑week strength program tailored to a true beginner training in a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull-up bar. The plan builds total-body strength with bodyweight progressions, intelligent volume increases, and clear standards to advance. It uses three phases to develop movement quality, strength, and density, with optional conditioning and simple nutrition/recovery guidance.

Overview
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week (e.g., Mon–Wed–Fri). Optional short conditioning on 1–2 other days.
- Session length: 35–55 minutes.
- Equipment: doorway pull-up bar, yoga mat, sturdy chair/sofa/coffee table (for dips/rows/elevated work), towel (for assisted pull-ups), backpack (load with books/water for added resistance later).
- Warm-up (10 minutes each session):
  - 3 minutes easy cardio (march in place/high knees/jump rope without rope).
  - Mobility: 6–8 reps each: cat–cow, hip circles, thoracic rotations, ankle rocks.
  - Activation: glute bridge 2x10, dead bug 2x6/side, scapular pull-ups 2x6 (hang and shrug), plank 20s.
- Tempo and control: Use a 3-1-1 tempo on main lifts early on (3 sec down, 1 sec pause where appropriate, 1 sec up). Progress to more explosive concentric while keeping controlled eccentrics.
- Rest: 60–120 sec between sets on main lifts; 30–60 sec on accessories and core.
- RPE guidance: Aim RPE 7–8 on work sets unless noted (leave 2–3 reps in reserve), increasing difficulty week to week via reps, sets, leverage, or load.

Progression anchors and substitutions
- Pulling options: Assisted pull-up (use a chair for foot support or loop a towel over bar and hold ends), eccentric-only pull-ups (jump up, 4–5s down), inverted row under table/chair setup or towel row anchored in door.
- Pushing options: Incline push-up (hands on counter/sofa), flat floor push-up, decline push-up (feet elevated).
- Squat/hinge options: Sit-to-stand, air squat, tempo squat, split squat, Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on chair), hip hinge/RDL patterning, hip thrust/glute bridge progressions, single-leg variations.
- Core/spine: Planks, side planks, hollow variations, anti-rotation (pallof-like with towel isometric in door), carry substitute: backpack front hold/braced marches.

Phase 1: Foundation and Movement Quality (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: Learn patterns, build joint tolerance, establish pulling/pushing/squatting basics, accumulate volume without excessive soreness. Focus on controlled eccentrics and midline stability.

Week structure: 3 full-body days (A/B rotating). Optional 1–2 short conditioning days: 15–20 min brisk walk, stair climbs, or low-impact circuits.

Week 1
- Day A
  1) Incline push-up (hands on counter/sofa): 4x6–8, 3-1-1 tempo
  2) Assisted pull-up (one foot on chair) or towel-assisted: 5x3–5, 3–4s eccentric
  3) Sit-to-stand to air squat progression: 4x8, 3s eccentric + 1s pause at bottom
  4) Hip bridge: 3x10–12, 2s squeeze at top
  5) Front plank: 3x20–30s
  6) Scapular pull-ups: 2x8
- Day B
  1) Flat push-up or higher incline if needed: 4x5–8
  2) Inverted row under sturdy table/desk or low bar alternative: 4x6–8
  3) Split squat (rear foot on floor): 3x6–8/leg, 3s eccentric
  4) Hip hinge pattern: dowel/broom handle or hands-on-hips RDL drill 3x10; then reverse lunges 2x6/leg
  5) Side plank: 3x20s/side
  6) Dead bug: 3x6/side

Week 2
- Increase reps by ~1–2/set where possible. Keep same exercises and tempos.
- Add one set to primary push and pull (becomes 5 sets).
- Core: progress holds by 5–10s.

Week 3
- Slight leverage progressions:
  - Lower your incline for push-ups by one step or elevate feet 10–20 cm if already on floor for a challenge.
  - Pulling: add 1–2 eccentric-only reps after each set (jump up, 4–5s down).
  - Squats: transition to air squats if all sets at 8+ quality reps last week; add 1s pause in the hole.
  - Bridges: single-leg bridge 3x8/leg.
- Volume: maintain 4–5 work sets on push/pull, 3–4 sets on legs.

Week 4
- Consolidate and test submax quality:
  - Push-ups: 3 sets to a technical 1–2 reps in reserve (AMRAP but stop shy of failure), record best set.
  - Pulling: 6–8 sets of 3 reps (cluster style) of assisted pull-ups focusing on crisp reps. Finish with 1–2 sets inverted rows 8–10.
  - Squat: 4x8–10 tempo air squats; add 2 sets Bulgarian split squats 6–8/leg.
  - Hinge: hip thrust/bridge feet elevated 3x10–12.
  - Core: hollow body hold progression 4x20–30s.

Phase 2: Strength Progression and Unilateral Emphasis (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: Build real strength via more challenging leverage, slower eccentrics where needed, unilateral leg work, and increasing pulling proficiency toward first strict pull-up.

Structure: 3 full-body days (A/B/C). Start using backpack load for squats/lunges/bridges when reps are easy at bodyweight.

Week 5
- Day A
  1) Push-up (flat) or decline if strong: 5x6–10
  2) Assisted pull-up (reduced assistance): 6x3–5; add 5s eccentric on last rep of each set
  3) Bulgarian split squat: 4x6–8/leg; hold backpack goblet-style if needed
  4) Hip thrust (shoulders on sofa): 4x8–12; add backpack on hips if needed
  5) Hollow body rocks or tuck hold: 3x20–30s
- Day B
  1) Pike push-up (hips high) or elevated decline push-up: 4x5–8
  2) Inverted row feet elevated or flat: 4x8–10
  3) Tempo air squat 3-1-1: 4x10; add backpack front hold when >10 easy
  4) Single-leg Romanian deadlift (bodyweight, balance-focused): 3x8/leg slow eccentric
  5) Side plank with top-leg raise: 3x20–30s/side
- Day C
  1) Mixed grip pull-up practice: 8–10 clusters of 2–3 reps assisted or eccentric; rest 45–60s
  2) Diamond or close-grip push-up: 4x6–10
  3) Step-back lunge or walking lunge in place: 4x8/leg; add backpack when ready
  4) Nordic hip hinge prep: slow good-morning pattern + glute bridge burnout 2x15
  5) Anti-rotation: towel isometric press in door frame 3x20s/side

Week 6
- Progress volume/leverages:
  - Push-ups: add 1 rep/set or small elevation of feet.
  - Pull-ups: introduce band if available; if not, keep reducing foot pressure. Try a single strict negative (8s down) 2–3 times in session A/C.
  - Legs: add backpack load 2–6 kg equivalent.
  - Core: add time or move to harder hollow progression.
- Finish one session with a 6–8 minute EMOM: 2–3 push-ups + 2 assisted pull-ups each minute (quality over fatigue).

Week 7
- Strength bias with lower reps:
  - Push-ups: 6x5–6 at harder leverage (RPE 8).
  - Pull-ups: 8x2–3 assisted at lowest help you can manage; test a chin-up hold at top for max 5–10s.
  - Bulgarians: 5x5–6/leg heavier (backpack).
  - Hip thrust: 4x8–10 heavier; 2s pause at top.
  - Core: RKC plank 3x15–20s + side plank 2x30s.

Week 8
- Consolidation/test week:
  - Test max quality push-ups in one set (stop with 1 rep in reserve).
  - Test strict chin-up ability: attempt 1 rep. If not yet, test longest top hold and longest eccentric (goal 10s).
  - Legs: AMRAP set on Bulgarian split squat at bodyweight or loaded (stop 1–2 shy of form break).
  - Reduce total sets by ~20% elsewhere to recover.

Phase 3: Strength Density and Pull-up Chase (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: Convert strength to higher quality volume, sharpen pulling toward first strict chin-up/pull-up, integrate denser sessions, and finish with clear benchmarks.

Structure: 3 days full-body with emphasis blocks, plus optional short conditioning.

Week 9
- Day A (Upper push emphasis, pull skill)
  1) Decline push-up or pseudo planche lean push-up: 6x5–8
  2) Chin-up clusters: 10x1–3 assisted or bodyweight negatives; 30–45s rest; aim total 15–25 quality reps
  3) Pike push-up: 3x6–8
  4) Inverted row feet elevated: 3x8–12
  5) Hollow to arch rocks: 3x12
- Day B (Lower strength)
  1) Bulgarian split squat heavy: 5x5/leg (backpack)
  2) Backpack front squat/zercher-style hold air squat: 4x8–10 with 2–3s eccentric
  3) Hip thrust heavy: 4x8–10, 2s pause
  4) Single-leg RDL: 3x8/leg
  5) Carry substitute: backpack front hold marches 3x30–45s
- Day C (Pull emphasis, push volume)
  1) Pull-up EMOM 10 min: odd minutes 2–3 assisted chin-ups; even minutes 1 long eccentric (6–8s) + 1 scap pull
  2) Push-up volume: 5x8–12 at challenging leverage
  3) Row variation: 3x10–12
  4) Core: side plank reach-through 3x10/side + dead bug 3x8/side

Week 10
- Progress by:
  - Reducing assistance further; attempt 1–2 singles at true bodyweight chin-up if close.
  - Adding slight load to push-ups (backpack on back) if at 12+ reps flat.
  - Adding 1 set to Bulgarians or increasing backpack load 10–20%.
  - EMOM becomes 12 minutes if recovery allows.

Week 11
- Intensification + micro-peak
  - Day A: Chin-up singles practice 8–12 attempts with full rest 60–90s. Each attempt: try strict rep; if fail, perform max top hold then 1 slow eccentric.
  - Day B: Bulgarian split squat 6x4/leg heavier; Hip thrust 5x6–8 heavier; finish with quad/hamstring isometric holds 2x20–30s.
  - Day C: Push-up ladder: 1-2-3-4-5-4-3-2-1 at chosen leverage with 30–40s rests; Pulling assistance volume 4x6–8 (rows), plus 3x3–4 assisted chins to keep pattern.
  - Core each day: mix hollow, RKC plank, anti-rotation.

Week 12 (Deload/test and consolidate)
- Reduce total working sets by ~30–40% and avoid failure.
- Tests and markers:
  - Chin-up/pull-up: Warm up shoulders, then 3–4 singles attempts across session. Log best outcome: strict rep, long top hold, or longest eccentric. Goal: 1st strict chin-up or a 12s controlled eccentric.
  - Push-ups: Max quality set (stop 1 rep shy of failure). Goal: 20+ strict if starting from incline, 10–15+ if on floor earlier.
  - Lower body: Bulgarian split squat AMRAP at prior Week 9–10 load, stop 1–2 in reserve; note rep PR.
- Light accessories only; mobility focus.

Weekly add-ons and conditioning (optional, 1–2x/week, 15–20 min)
- Option 1: Low-impact circuit 3–4 rounds (no failure): jumping jacks 30s, march/jog in place 60s, air squats 12, incline push-ups 8–10, dead bug 6/side. Rest 60–90s between rounds.
- Option 2: Stair/climb/walk intervals: 5 min easy warm-up, then 6–10 rounds 30s brisk + 60s easy, finish 3 min easy.
- Keep these 24+ hours away from leg-focused days if they feel fatiguing.

Recovery and mobility
- Daily 5–8 min movement snack: thoracic openers, hip flexor stretch 2x30s/side, calf/ankle rocks, wrist prep for push-ups.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours. Keep a consistent schedule.
- Soreness rule: mild/moderate is okay; sharp pain or joint pain is not. Modify ranges and regress leverages as needed.
- Deload signals: If performance drops for 2 consecutive sessions or you feel unusually fatigued, cut sets by 30% for the week.

Nutrition basics for strength and body recomposition
- Protein: target 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day, spread over 3–4 meals. Include a palm-sized portion each meal.
- Calories: If body comp goal is neutral or slow recomposition, eat at maintenance to slight surplus on training days (+200 kcal) and maintenance to slight deficit on rest days (−0 to −200 kcal).
- Carbs pre-training: a fist-sized serving 60–90 minutes before (oats, fruit, rice, bread) and hydrate well.
- Post-training: protein-rich meal within 2 hours; add carbs if the next session is within 36 hours.
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day; add 500 ml around training.
- Micronutrients: 2–3 servings fruit + 2–3 servings veg daily; add 1–2 servings dairy or fortified alternatives for calcium; consider vitamin D3 if limited sun exposure (consult a professional).

Technique cues and standards
- Push-ups: Body in a straight line, elbows ~30–45° from torso, chest to fist height or floor, full lockout.
- Pull-ups/chin-ups: Full hang (scaps set), pull chest toward bar, chin clearly over bar, controlled lower to full hang.
- Squats: Feet shoulder width, knees track over toes, depth to thighs at least parallel with control.
- Bulgarians: Slight forward torso, front knee tracks over toes, back knee down with control, drive through front mid-foot.
- Hip thrusts: Posterior pelvic tilt at top, ribcage down, pause and squeeze glutes.

Tracking and progression notes
- Keep a simple log: exercises, sets/reps, assistance level, RPE, and any notes on technique.
- Progress by one variable at a time: reduce assistance or increase leverage before adding lots of volume.
- The primary milestone is a first strict chin-up. Expect many to achieve it by Weeks 10–12 with consistent practice and appropriate bodyweight management.

This plan gives your beginner a serious, progressive path to real strength with only a pull-up bar and a mat, while maintaining safety, measurable goals, and clear weekly structure.

Here’s a simple, sustainable 12-week nutrition plan to support beginner strength gains, recovery, and potential body recomposition. It’s flexible and habit-based so he can follow it from a small flat without elaborate cooking.

Assumptions and targets
- Goal: Build strength, support recovery, and improve body composition (slow recomposition or slight lean gain).
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day.
- Calories: Maintenance to a slight surplus (+150–250 kcal/day). If he wants to lean out a bit, keep most days at maintenance and add the surplus on training days only.
- Carbs: Moderate-to-high on training days, moderate on rest days.
- Fats: Moderate, mainly unsaturated.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day.
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day + ~500 ml around training.

Step 1: Establish maintenance and macros
- Estimate maintenance: bodyweight (kg) x 30–33 for a starting point. Track weight and adjust after 10–14 days.
- Macros framework (example for 75 kg male; scale up/down by bodyweight):
  - Protein: 120–165 g/day (aim for 30–40 g per meal across 3–4 meals).
  - Fat: 0.7–1.0 g/kg (50–75 g/day) from olive oil, nuts, seeds, eggs, fatty fish, dairy.
  - Carbs: Fill remaining calories (typically 2–4 g/kg; 150–300 g/day depending on total calories and goal).

Training vs. rest day approach
- Training days: Maintenance +150–250 kcal, carbs on the higher end (include a pre- and post-workout carb portion).
- Rest days: Maintenance or −0 to −150 kcal with slightly lower carbs and a touch more veggies and fats.
- Keep protein consistent every day.

Meal timing basics
- Pre-workout (60–120 min before): 30–60 g carbs + 20–35 g protein. Example: Greek yogurt with fruit and honey; or turkey sandwich; or oats with whey.
- Post-workout (within 2 hours): 25–40 g protein + 40–80 g carbs. Example: rice + chicken + veg; or wrap with tuna/beans; or chocolate milk + banana.
- If training fasted is necessary: take 20–30 g whey or a high-protein yogurt beforehand and prioritize a solid post-workout meal.

12-week habit progression
Weeks 1–2: Foundation habits
- Hit protein at each meal (30–40 g).
- Build a simple plate: 1–2 palms protein, 1–2 fists veg, 1 fist carbs (2 on training days), 1–2 thumbs fats.
- Hydration: Start day with 300–500 ml water; carry a bottle; clear/light-yellow urine goal.
- Grocery basics: eggs, Greek yogurt/skyr, cottage cheese, chicken/thighs, canned tuna/salmon/beans, tofu/tempeh, rice, oats, wholegrain bread/wraps, potatoes, olive oil, nuts, frozen veg, salad mixes, fruit, dark chocolate.

Weeks 3–4: Consistency and fiber
- Hit 25–35 g fiber/day: fruit 2–3 servings + veg 2–3 servings; include legumes 3–4x/week.
- Add a pre/post training carb-protein pairing on workout days.
- Portion awareness: use hand portions to avoid weighing if he prefers. If using a scale, weigh main starches/proteins at dinner to calibrate eyeballing.

Weeks 5–6: Calorie calibration
- Weigh trends: average daily weight across the week.
  - If weight is flat and strength is rising: stay the course.
  - If under-recovering or stalling: add +150 kcal/day (roughly +30–40 g carbs).
  - If gaining >0.25–0.5 kg/week unintentionally: reduce −150 kcal/day.
- Alcohol: max 3–4 drinks/week; none within 24 hours of hard lower-body sessions if possible.

Weeks 7–8: Protein quality and micronutrients
- Include 2–3 oily fish servings/week or supplement omega-3 if not eating fish (discuss with a professional).
- Vitamin D3 if limited sun (per local guidelines; consult a professional).
- Aim for a rainbow of vegetables across the week for micronutrient diversity.
- Pre-sleep protein: 20–40 g casein-rich source (skyr/Greek yogurt/cottage cheese) on most nights to support recovery.

Weeks 9–10: Performance fueling
- Training days: ensure a carb source both pre- and post-workout. If sessions feel flat, bump pre-workout carbs by ~20–30 g (add a banana or extra toast).
- Creatine monohydrate (optional, evidence-based): 3–5 g daily, any time, with adequate fluids. Expect 1–2 kg water-weight increase; strength/recovery benefits accrue over 2–4 weeks.

Weeks 11–12: Dial in and test
- Keep meals familiar and easily digestible in test/deload week.
- Slightly reduce fiber 2–3 hours pre-workout if he gets GI discomfort (choose low-fiber carbs like white rice or sourdough).
- Maintain hydration and sodium (salt meals to taste), especially if sweating more.

Simple meal templates (mix and match)
- Breakfasts
  - Greek yogurt/skyr + oats or granola + berries + honey.
  - Eggs (2–4) + wholegrain toast + fruit; add spinach/tomatoes.
  - Protein smoothie: whey/plant protein + milk/alt + banana + oats + peanut butter.

- Lunches
  - Wrap: chicken/turkey/tofu + mixed salad + hummus + wholegrain wrap.
  - Rice bowl: microwave rice + tuna/beans + frozen veg + olive oil/soy sauce.
  - Omelette + potatoes or toast + side salad.

- Dinners
  - Stir-fry: frozen veg mix + tofu/chicken + rice/noodles + sauce.
  - Baked tray: chicken thighs + potatoes + carrots/onions; olive oil + spices.
  - Chili: lean mince or beans + tomatoes + spices; serve with rice.

- Snacks
  - Fruit + handful of nuts.
  - Cottage cheese or skyr + fruit.
  - Protein bar/shake when convenience is key.
  - Wholegrain toast + peanut butter + banana.

Portion guide by hand (easy, no-scale)
- Protein: 1–2 palms/meal (30–40 g).
- Carbs: 1 fist/meal (rest days), 1–2 fists/meal (training days).
- Fats: 1–2 thumbs/meal.
- Veg: 1–2 fists/meal.

Budget/time tips for a small flat
- Use frozen veg and pre-cooked microwave grains.
- Batch-cook proteins (bake chicken thighs, boil eggs).
- Keep canned fish/beans on hand.
- Season simply: salt, pepper, garlic, curry paste, soy sauce.
- Use a mini rice cooker or microwave for simple prep.

Monitoring and adjustments
- Track three things weekly: average bodyweight, session energy (1–10), and recovery soreness/sleep quality.
- If two of three trend down for 2+ weeks, add 150–250 kcal/day (mostly carbs).
- If bodyweight increases faster than intended, remove 150–200 kcal/day (carbs/fats) while keeping protein stable.
- Keep changes modest and wait 10–14 days before the next tweak.

Non-negotiables
- Protein at each meal.
- Pre/post workout fuel on training days.
- 7–9 hours of sleep and 2–3 L water/day (more if heavier or hot weather).
- Vegetables or fruit at most meals.

This plan pairs cleanly with the 12-week program: steady protein, smart carbs around training, and simple habits that build recovery and strength without complexity.

Here’s a home-friendly cardio add-on that fits the 12-week strength plan, requires no equipment beyond the mat and space, and won’t interfere with strength gains. It uses low-impact options plus short, higher-intensity intervals when appropriate. Place cardio 24+ hours away from lower-body–heavy strength sessions when possible. Keep at least one full rest day per week.

General guidelines
- Frequency: 2–3 cardio sessions/week (start with 2 for Weeks 1–4; move to 2–3 in Weeks 5–12).
- Duration: 15–25 minutes/session early; up to 30 minutes later if recovery is good.
- Intensity: Use RPE 1–10 scale.
  - Easy/recovery: RPE 3–4 (nasal-breathing conversational pace).
  - Moderate steady: RPE 5–6.
  - Intervals: Work bouts RPE 7–9, recovery RPE 3–4.
- Warm-up (5 minutes each session): easy marching in place, arm circles, ankle hops, hip openers, 2–3 short 10–15s pick-ups.

Menu of at-home cardio options
- Low impact (great for neighbors/floors): brisk marching in place, step-back lunges, alternating toe taps to a step, shadow boxing, low-impact jacks (step out instead of jump), bear crawl or high plank shoulder taps.
- Moderate impact (if floors/neighbors allow): jumping jacks, high knees, jump rope without rope, skater hops, mountain climbers, squat-to-calf-raise.
- Stair option (if building stairs available): brisk stair walks and controlled descents.

12-week cardio structure
Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Build base and consistency (2x/week, 15–20 min)
- Session A: Low-impact steady
  - 15–20 min at RPE 4–5 using a mix: 2 min brisk march + 1 min shadow boxing + 1 min step-back lunges (alternating) + 1 min toe taps. Loop continuously. Focus on nasal breathing and posture.
- Session B: Intro intervals (low impact)
  - 5 min warm-up
  - 8 rounds: 30s “work” at RPE 7 (fast marching/high knees without jumping or brisk shadow boxing combos) + 45s easy march (RPE 3–4)
  - 2–3 min easy cool-down
- Optional finisher on a strength day (only if recovery is good): 5–8 minutes EMOM of 20–30s low-impact jacks + remaining minute easy march. Keep it easy-moderate.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progress volume or intensity (2–3x/week, 20–25 min)
Pick two of the three sessions weekly; add the third if recovery is solid.

- Session C: Tempo steady state
  - 5 min warm-up
  - 12–16 min continuous at RPE 5–6 rotating every 2 min: low-impact jacks, shadow boxing, toe taps, marching with arm drive.
  - 2–3 min cool-down and light mobility.

- Session D: Mixed intervals
  - 5 min warm-up with 3 x 10s pick-ups
  - 6–10 rounds: 40s work at RPE 7–8 (mountain climbers, skater steps/hops, fast toe taps) + 40–60s easy march
  - 2–3 min cool-down

- Session E: Stair session (if available; otherwise substitute Session C)
  - 5 min warm-up
  - 10–15 min continuous: climb 1–3 flights at brisk walk, descend easy; keep RPE 5–6.
  - 2–3 min cool-down; calf/hip flexor stretch.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Density or longer easy work (2–3x/week, 20–30 min)
Choose one interval day and one steady day; the third is optional.

- Session F: Ladder intervals
  - 5 min warm-up
  - Ladder 20–40–60–40–20s work at RPE 8 (choose: high knees, shadow boxing flurries, mountain climbers) with equal-time easy recovery after each.
  - Repeat the ladder 1–2 times based on recovery (aim total working time 8–12 min).
  - 3 min cool-down.

- Session G: Longer easy aerobic
  - 5 min warm-up
  - 15–20 min continuous at RPE 4–5 using a smooth circuit: march → toe taps → shadow boxing → step-back lunges (no jumping). Breathe through the nose as much as possible.
  - 3 min cool-down and mobility.

- Session H: Threshold taste (only if joints feel good; otherwise do Session G)
  - 5 min warm-up
  - 3–4 x 3 min at RPE 6–7 with 2 min easy between. Use non-jumping moves that let you sustain pace (fast marching with arm drive, shadow boxing combos).
  - 3 min cool-down.

Placement with strength days
- Example weekly layout (when lifting Mon–Wed–Fri):
  - Mon: Strength
  - Tue: Cardio (Session A/C/G)
  - Wed: Strength
  - Thu: Off or light mobility
  - Fri: Strength
  - Sat: Cardio (Session B/D/F/H)
  - Sun: Off or easy walk/mobility
- If only two cardio slots fit, prioritize one steady (G or C) and one interval (F or D).

Low-impact HIIT option (8–12 min, handy if short on time)
- Warm-up 3 min
- 10 rounds: 20s hard (RPE 8–9) shadow boxing flurry + 40s easy march
- Cool-down 2 min
Use sparingly (1x/week) and avoid the day before heavy lower-body sessions.

Heart rate and progression cues
- Rough HR targets: easy RPE 4 ≈ 60–70% max HR; intervals at RPE 7–9 ≈ 75–90% max HR if he tracks HR.
- Progress one variable at a time each week: add 1–2 minutes total, or add 1–2 rounds, or nudge intensity slightly while keeping form crisp.
- Stop if pain, dizziness, or unusual breathlessness occurs; regress to lower-impact options.

Recovery considerations
- Keep interval days at least 24 hours from Bulgarian split squat–heavy sessions.
- If leg DOMS is high, swap in upper-body–biased cardio (shadow boxing, low-impact jacks, marching with arm drive) and skip climbers/skaters that load quads/hips.
- Maintain hydration and a small carb snack 60–90 minutes before intervals for best quality.

This add-on keeps conditioning effective, joint-friendly, and compatible with the strength focus, with clear progressions and multiple options that fit a small flat.

Great question. For a small flat, think “maximum versatility per square meter.” Here’s a staged buy-list that complements his current bar + mat setup and scales his strength work for years without a full gym.

Tier 1: Immediate best value (compact, high impact)

Tier 2: Strength progression and loading options (still compact)

- Compact sandbag (20–40 kg, fillable): Bear-hug squats, shouldering, cleans, carries, drags; very apartment-friendly and versatile for conditioning.

Nice-to-have accessories
- Hip circle/minibands: Glute activation, knee tracking, warm-ups.
- Ab wheel: Cheap, very effective core intensifier (use with care).
- Yoga blocks/wedges: Wrist comfort, incline/decline push-up tweaks, ankle mobility.
- Floor sliders or small towels: Hamstring curls, body saws, slide lunges on hard floors.

Selection tips by goal and space
- Upper-body strength focus: Rings/suspension trainer + adjustable dumbbells first.
- Lower-body loading without a rack: One heavy kettlebell or sandbag for goblet/front-loaded squats and hinges.
- Progressive micro-loading: Loadable dumbbell handles + small plates.

Suggested purchase sequence (budget-conscious)
1) Bands set with door anchor.
2) Rings/suspension trainer.
3) Adjustable dumbbells (to at least 20 kg per hand if possible).
4) One heavy kettlebell (20–24 kg; 16 kg if needed).
5) Dip belt or sturdy loading strap.
6) Foldable bench or sandbag, depending on preference.

Safety/fit checks for a small flat
- Doorway pull-up bar must be solid before hanging rings or using a dip belt—test incrementally.
- Mind neighbors: choose low-impact moves (swings in control, no dropping weights).

With this setup, your client can progress from beginner to advanced strength work, load all major patterns, and keep sessions varied—without turning the flat into a gym.

Got it—let’s turn Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) into a higher-intensity block without breaking recovery. We’ll keep three full-body days but: lower reps on primaries, add harder leverages/partials/pauses, introduce density sets and EMOMs, and set clear weekly progression targets. Rest periods lengthen slightly on heavy work, and we’ll use RPE 8–9 on primaries. Cardio stays easy/moderate on adjacent days.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) — Intensified Strength Block
Structure
- Days: 3 full-body sessions (A/B/C).
- Primaries: Push, Pull, Single-leg, Hinge.
- Intensity: RPE 8–9 on primaries; accessories RPE 7–8.
- Rest: 90–150s on primaries; 45–75s on accessories.
- Progression rule: Each week, progress one variable per lift (leverage, reps, or set count). If you miss targets 2+ sessions, hold or back off assistance/volume by 10–20%.

Week 5
- Day A (Heavy push + pull strength)
  1) Push-up (choose the hardest leverage that allows 4–6 reps: flat → feet-elevated 20–40 cm or backpack 5–10 kg): 6x4–6, full ROM, 2–3s eccentric, 1s pause near bottom.
  2) Assisted chin-up (minimal foot pressure; mix neutral/underhand): 7x3, 5s eccentric on last rep/set.
  3) Bulgarian split squat (front-loaded with backpack if possible): 5x5/leg, 2s pause at bottom.
  4) Hip thrust (shoulders on sofa, backpack load): 4x6–8, 2s squeeze at top.
  5) Core: Hollow body hold or tuck-to-hollow rocks 4x25–35s.

- Day B (Leg density + vertical pull skill)
  1) Tempo air squat or backpack front squat: 4x8 at 3–1–X tempo (explode up).
  2) Chin-up density EMOM 10 min: 2 assisted reps each minute (quality, full hang).
  3) Pike push-up or decline push-up: 5x5–7.
  4) Single-leg RDL (slow 3s down): 3x8/leg.
  5) Side plank with reach-through: 3x25–30s/side.

- Day C (Upper push volume + pull eccentric)
  1) Push-up cluster sets: 5 clusters of 6 total reps at hard leverage (e.g., 2+2+2 with 20s intra-set rest). Aim RPE 9 by last cluster.
  2) Chin-up eccentric ladders: 4 ladders of 3 reps with descending eccentric times (8s, 6s, 4s). Rest 90s between ladders.
  3) Step-back lunge (loaded if possible): 4x8/leg.
  4) Hip hinge pattern + glute bridge burnout: 2x15 slow good-mornings (bodyweight cueing) + 2x15–20 glute bridges.
  5) Anti-rotation towel press in door frame: 3x20–25s/side.

Week 6 — Progression focus: leverage up on push, reduce assistance on pull
- Day A
  1) Push-up: 6x5–6 at tougher leverage (raise feet or add +2–3 kg to backpack). Keep the 1s bottom pause.
  2) Assisted chin-up: 8x3; add 1–2 reps total across workout or extend eccentric to 6s on final rep of first 4 sets.
  3) Bulgarian split squat: 5x6/leg (same load or +1 rep/set).
  4) Hip thrust: 4x6–8 (add load or pause 3s top on last set).
  5) Core: Hollow rocks 4x12–16.

- Day B
  1) Backpack front squat: 5x6–8 at 3–1–X tempo (slightly heavier than Week 5).
  2) Chin-up EMOM 12 min: alternate minutes 2 reps + 1 scapular pull; keep total quality.
  3) Pike push-up: 5x6–8.
  4) Single-leg RDL: 4x6–8/leg, add range or tempo.
  5) Side plank with top-leg raise: 3x25–35s/side.

- Day C
  1) Push-up cluster: 6 clusters (maintain leverage; aim to add 1 rep across clusters vs Week 5).
  2) Chin-up negatives: 5x2 reps at 8–10s eccentric; finish with 1–2 assisted singles.
  3) Walking/step-back lunge: 4x9–10/leg.
  4) Hip thrust pump: 3x12 (1s up/1s hold/1s down).
  5) Anti-rotation towel press: 3x25–30s/side.

Week 7 — Intensification (heaviest week)
- Day A (Heavy push/pull)
  1) Push-up (hard leverage): 7x3–5, 3s eccentric, 1s pause; RPE 9 on last two sets.
  2) Chin-up strength: 10x2 assisted at the lowest help possible. Between sets, 1 scapular pull.
  3) Bulgarian split squat: 6x4–5/leg heavy (long rest).
  4) Hip thrust: 5x5–6 heavy with 2s pause.
  5) Core: RKC plank 4x15–20s.

- Day B (Density + threshold)
  1) Backpack front squat: 4x8 at 2–0–X; last set AMRAP to 1–2 reps in reserve.
  2) Pull-up EMOM 10–12 min: 2 reps odd minutes; 1 long eccentric (8–10s) even minutes.
  3) Pike push-up deficit (hands on yoga blocks/books): 4x5–6.
  4) Single-leg RDL: 3x8/leg with 2s bottom pause for balance/control.
  5) Side plank hip taps: 3x12–15/side.

- Day C (Contrast + clusters)
  1) Push-up contrast set x5 rounds: 4 heavy reps (decline/backpack) + 6 speed reps (flat, fast but crisp). Rest 2 min between rounds.
  2) Chin-up ladder: 1–2–3 assisted reps x 3 ladders; after each ladder add 1 slow eccentric (6–8s).
  3) Split squat: 4x8/leg moderate, smooth tempo.
  4) Hip bridge iso hold: 2x45–60s then 1x20 reps pumps.
  5) Anti-rotation: 3x25–30s/side.

Week 8 — Consolidation + mini-test (not a deload; slightly lower total volume, high quality)
- Day A
  1) Push-up test set at hardest leverage: 1 top set to 1–2 reps in reserve, then 3x4 back-off sets at ~90% difficulty.
  2) Chin-up singles practice: 6–8 attempts with 75–90s rest. If no strict rep yet, do top hold max (up to 10s) then 1 slow eccentric each attempt.
  3) Bulgarian split squat: 4x6/leg solid, no grind.
  4) Hip thrust: 3x6–8 with perfect pauses.

- Day B
  1) Backpack front squat: 3x8 easy-moderate (technique focus).
  2) Chin-up density: EMOM 8–10 min, 2 reps each minute with pristine form.
  3) Pike push-up: 4x6–8 smooth.
  4) Single-leg RDL: 3x8/leg.
  5) Core of choice: 3 sets.

- Day C
  1) Push-up cluster: 4 clusters totaling 16–24 quality reps.
  2) Chin-up negatives: 3x2 long eccentrics (8–10s). Finish with 2x6–8 inverted rows for volume.
  3) Lunge pattern: 3x8/leg.
  4) Hip bridge pump: 2x20.
  5) Mobility and soft-tissue: 8–10 minutes.

Notes, cues, and safeguards
- Technique integrity: Maintain full ROM and rigid trunk on push-ups; full hang, chest-up path, and controlled lower on chins.
- Assistance scaling: Use the least foot pressure or the longest towel to reduce help; log “assistance level” each session.
- Backpack loading: Add small, frequent jumps (books/water). Secure load to prevent shifting on push-ups.
- Recovery: Keep cardio easy (RPE 3–5) this block. Sleep 7–9 hours; pre/post workout carbs as in the nutrition plan.
- Pain rule: Joint pain or sharp pain = regress leverage/ROM; muscular burn is fine.
- Targets by end of Week 8:
  - Push-ups: 6–10 solid reps at decline/backpack, or 15–20 on floor.
  - Chin-up: 1 strict chin-up for many; otherwise a 10–12s controlled eccentric and 5–8 assisted doubles.
  - Bulgarians: Strong sets of 5–6/leg with front load.

This ups Phase 2’s intensity with heavier leverages, clusters, pauses, and EMOM density—driving faster strength gains while staying recoverable in a small-flat setup.

Here’s a Saturday “Finisher Day” that’s fun, fast, and flexible. It won’t beat him up or interfere with Monday’s strength, but it’ll scratch the itch to move. Choose one of the three formats each Saturday based on mood and energy. Total time: 20–30 minutes including warm-up and cool-down. Keep 1 full rest day on Sunday.

General rules
- Warm-up (5 minutes): easy march or shadow boxing, arm circles, hip openers, 2 x 10s pick-ups.
- Effort: Aim RPE 6–8 overall; finish feeling energized, not wrecked.
- Space/noise friendly: low-impact variants provided.
- Cool-down (3–5 minutes): brisk walk in place, breathing drills (4s in, 6s out), light mobility.

Option 1: Bodyweight Gauntlet (EMOM mash-up, 20 minutes)
- Minutes 1–5: EMOM 5 rounds
  - 6–10 push-ups (choose incline/flat/decline) + 20s shadow boxing flurry
- Minutes 6–10: EMOM 5 rounds
  - 2–4 assisted chin-ups or 1 slow eccentric (6–8s) + 15–20 mountain climbers (low-impact: slow climbers)
- Minutes 11–15: EMOM 5 rounds
  - 8–12 split squats/leg alternating each minute (low-impact jacks or toe taps between legs if time)
- Minutes 16–20: EMOM 5 rounds
  - 20–30s hollow hold or dead bug + 20–30s brisk march/high knees (no jump)
Notes: Keep 10–15s spare each minute; scale reps to maintain quality.

Option 2: “Deck of Cards” Play (15–25 minutes)
- Use a standard deck or app. Set a 20-minute cap.
- Suits = moves, card value = reps (A = 11, face cards = 10, jokers = 15 reps of any move).
  - Hearts: Push-ups (scale leverage)
  - Spades: Assisted pull-ups or inverted rows (3–6 reps per draw; if you draw a high card twice in a row, swap one to 6–8s negatives)
  - Diamonds: Split squats (per leg = half the card; e.g., 8 = 4/leg)
  - Clubs: Toe-tap flurries or low-impact jacks (card x 2 seconds, e.g., 7 = 14s)
- Pace: Move steadily, rest as needed to keep form. Stop at the cap or when deck is done.

Option 3: Rings/Bar Playground (if he adds rings; otherwise use bar + floor)
Circuit for 4–6 rounds, 45s work/15s rest per station (20–30 minutes):
- Station 1: Ring rows or bar inverted rows (angle as hard as manageable)
- Station 2: Push-up variation (feet-elevated or deficit on books; or ring push-ups)
- Station 3: Split squat jumps (low-impact: split squat to calf raise) or skater steps
- Station 4: Hollow rocks or rollout substitute (ring fallouts or plank walkouts)
- Station 5: Shadow boxing combos (jab–cross–hook–roll) or fast marching with arm drive
Rest 60–90s between rounds. Keep reps snappy, stopping 1–2 shy of failure.

Themed Saturdays by phase
- Weeks 1–4 (learning): Choose Option 1 with lower reps and focus on tempo and crisp technique.
- Weeks 5–8 (intensified): Use Option 2 for fun randomness; cap at 20 min to protect recovery.
- Weeks 9–12 (density): Use Option 3 or Option 1 with tougher leverages; aim to keep heart rate high without sloppy reps.

Quick alternatives (10–12 minutes) if time/energy is low
- Shadow box finisher: 6 rounds 45s on/15s off; switch stance each round; core tight.
- Chipper: 30 push-ups (scaled), 40 toe taps/side, 30 split squats/leg, 40 mountain climbers/side, 60s hollow. Break into mini-sets as needed.

Safety and scaling
- Always stop 1–2 reps before form breaks, especially on pull-ups/negatives.
- Keep noise in check: pick low-impact options if you have neighbors below.
- If legs are very sore, swap lower-body moves for extra core/shadow boxing.

This Saturday finisher keeps things playful, varied, and effective—adding a touch of conditioning and skill practice without derailing strength progress.

Here’s a simple, repeatable mobility routine that fits the program and a small flat. It’s split into Daily Micro (5–8 min), Pre‑Lift Warm‑up (10 min), and Two Deeper Sessions (15–20 min) you can use 1–2x/week. No equipment beyond the mat; optional towel/doorframe.

Daily micro-mobility (5–8 minutes)
Use mornings or before bed—slow, nasal breathing.
- Breathing + ribcage: 90/90 hip lift with reach (feet on wall or sofa) 2x5 breaths. Exhale fully, ribs down; light posterior pelvic tilt.
- Spine/shoulders: Cat–cow 6–8 reps, then thoracic openers 6/side (thread the needle or open book).
- Hips/ankles: Hip CARs 3/side (slow controlled circles), ankle rocks 10/side (knee over toes, heel down).
- Hips/glutes: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch 2x25–30s/side (glute squeeze).
- Wrists: Wrist rocks 6–8 each direction (hands/fists, fingers forward/back).

Pre-lift mobility warm-up (10 minutes)
Do this before strength sessions to prep joints and raise temp. Move continuously, crisp but controlled.
- 2–3 minutes: Marching in place with arm swings + light shadow boxing.
- Dynamic sequence (1 round, 6–8 reps each):
  - World’s greatest stretch: lunge → elbow to instep → T-spine rotation (both directions).
  - Squat pry: deep bodyweight squat, elbows inside knees, gentle side-to-side shifts.
  - Hip airplane (supported on chair or wall): 4 reps/side.
  - Scapular sequence: 6 scapular pull-ups on the bar + 10 band/air pull-aparts + 6 shoulder circles each way.
  - Ankles/calves: elevated calf rocks or knee-over-toe rocks 10/side.
  - Core brace primer: dead bug 4/side + front plank 20–30s.

Post-session cool-down (3–5 minutes, optional)
- Easy nasal breathing walk in place 1–2 minutes.
- Quick resets: child’s pose with side reach 30s/side, doorway pec stretch 30s/side, hip flexor stretch 30s/side.

Deep-dive mobility Session A (15–20 minutes) — hips/ankles/low back
Use on Tue or Sat after cardio, or Sunday.
- Segmental cat-cow: 2x5 slow reps, focus on moving one vertebra at a time.
- 90/90 hip switches: 2x6 slow transitions, tall torso. Add forward fold 20–30s each side.
- Half-kneeling hip flexor with side-bend and posterior tilt: 2x30s/side.
- Pigeon or elevated figure‑4 stretch (on sofa): 2x30–45s/side; breathe into glute.
- Cossack squat (assisted holding doorframe): 2x6/side with 2s pause in the bottom.
- Ankles: knee-to-wall test and mobilization 2x10/side; finish with 30s calf stretch straight + 30s bent-knee/side.
- Lumbar decompression: hang from bar 2x20–30s (or long child’s pose 45–60s).

Deep-dive mobility Session B (15–20 minutes) — shoulders/T‑spine/wrists
Use on Thu or Sun.
- Foamless T‑spine extension over towel roll/pillow: 2x6 breaths at 2–3 spots.
- Thread the needle: 2x6/side with 2s pause.
- Doorway pec stretch (high and low angles): 2x30s/side each angle.
- Lat opener: kneeling prayer stretch on chair/sofa (palms up), allow ribs down: 2x30–45s.
- Scapular control: 2 rounds
  - Scapular wall slides 8 reps (back/head/ribs against wall).
  - Prone Y‑T‑W on floor 6 reps each (light, slow).
- Wrist sequence: palm/fingers forward rocks 8, fingers back rocks 8, palm-up stretch 20s, gentle fist circles 10/side.

Mini “movement snacks” (1–2 minutes, anytime)
- Desk break: 10 air squats + 10 band/air pull-aparts + 5 deep breaths.
- Hips reset: 60s squat sit hold (use doorframe for support), sway gently.
- Shoulders: 8–10 scap shrugs hanging from the bar (or dead hang if comfortable).

Programming notes
- Frequency: Daily micro + pre-lift warm-up every strength day; deep-dive A and/or B 1–2x/week.
- Progression: Increase hold times by 5–10s or add a second set; aim for smoother, larger pain-free ranges, not forced depth.
- Breath and bracing: Exhale fully on stretches to let ribs drop; keep light core tension on dynamic moves.
- Pain rule: Mild stretch sensation is fine; sharp or nerve-like pain is not—back off range or choose a gentler variant.
- Pull-up prep emphasis: Don’t skip scapular pulls, lat opener, and pec stretch—better overhead mechanics accelerate pull-up progress.
- Lower-body recovery: On heavy Bulgarian/squat weeks, prioritize Session A to keep hips/ankles happy.

This routine keeps joints happy, improves positions for squats/push-ups/pull-ups, and fits seamlessly around training in a small flat.

Here’s the complete 12-week plan summary for your beginner client training in a small flat with a pull-up bar and mat, including strength (with intensified Phase 2), cardio, Saturday finisher options, nutrition, and mobility. Use three strength days/week (e.g., Mon–Wed–Fri), cardio 2–3x/week, Saturday finisher, and at least one full rest day (Sun).

Structure at a glance
- Strength: 3x/week, 35–55 min. Phases: Foundation (Weeks 1–4), Intensified Strength (Weeks 5–8), Strength Density & Pull-up Chase (Weeks 9–12).
- Cardio: 2–3x/week, 15–30 min, low-impact options.
- Saturday finisher: 20–30 min fun session (choose one of 3 formats).
- Mobility: Daily micro (5–8 min), 10-min pre-lift warm-up, 1–2 deep sessions/week.
- Nutrition: Maintenance to slight surplus, high-protein, carbs around training.
- Equipment: Pull-up bar, mat; optional chair/sofa/table; backpack for load.

Phase 1 — Foundation and Movement Quality (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: Learn movement patterns; build tolerance; start pull-up pathway; accumulate volume without soreness. RPE 7–8, 3-1-1 tempo on primaries early.

Weekly format: 3 full-body days (A/B rotate). Warm-up 10 min; rests 60–120s main, 30–60s accessory.

Week 1
- Day A
  - Incline push-up 4x6–8 (controlled)
  - Assisted pull-up 5x3–5 (3–4s eccentrics)
  - Sit-to-stand → air squat 4x8 (3s down + 1s pause)
  - Hip bridge 3x10–12 (2s squeeze)
  - Front plank 3x20–30s
  - Scapular pull-ups 2x8
- Day B
  - Push-up (flat or incline) 4x5–8
  - Inverted row 4x6–8
  - Split squat 3x6–8/leg (3s down)
  - Hinge drill 3x10 + reverse lunge 2x6/leg
  - Side plank 3x20s/side
  - Dead bug 3x6/side

Week 2
- Add 1–2 reps/set where possible; +1 set to primary push/pull; core holds +5–10s. Same exercises/tempos.

Week 3
- Progress leverage:
  - Push-ups: lower incline or light feet-elevated if strong.
  - Pulls: add 1–2 eccentric-only reps after each set.
  - Squats: full air squats with 1s pause if ready.
  - Bridges: single-leg bridge 3x8/leg.
- Keep 4–5 sets push/pull, 3–4 sets legs.

Week 4 (Consolidate/mini-test)
- Push-ups: 3 sets to 1–2 reps in reserve; log best.
- Pulls: 6–8 x 3 assisted (clusters), finish 1–2 sets inverted rows 8–10.
- Squat: 4x8–10 tempo air squats + Bulgarian split squat 2x6–8/leg.
- Bridge: feet-elevated 3x10–12.
- Core: Hollow hold 4x20–30s.

Phase 2 — Intensified Strength Block (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: Push intensity; drive pull-up strength; progress unilateral leg strength. RPE 8–9 primaries; 90–150s rest.

Week 5
- Day A (Heavy push/pull)
  - Push-up (hardest leverage allowing 4–6) 6x4–6, 2–3s down, 1s pause
  - Assisted chin-up 7x3 (5s eccentric last rep/set)
  - Bulgarian split squat 5x5/leg (pause 2s bottom)
  - Hip thrust 4x6–8 (2s squeeze)
  - Hollow hold/rocks 4x25–35s
- Day B (Leg density + pull skill)
  - Tempo backpack front squat or air squat 4x8 at 3–1–X
  - Chin-up EMOM 10 min: 2 assisted reps each minute
  - Pike or decline push-up 5x5–7
  - Single-leg RDL 3x8/leg (3s down)
  - Side plank reach-through 3x25–30s/side
- Day C (Push clusters + pull eccentrics)
  - Push-up clusters: 5 clusters of 6 total reps (e.g., 2+2+2, 20s intra-rest)
  - Chin-up eccentric ladders: 4x(3 reps at 8s/6s/4s lowers)
  - Step-back lunge 4x8/leg
  - Hinge drill + glute bridge 2x15 each
  - Anti-rotation towel press 3x20–25s/side

Week 6 (Leverage up; reduce assistance)
- Day A: Push-up 6x5–6 harder leverage; Chins 8x3 (longer eccentrics on early sets); Bulgarians 5x6/leg; Hip thrust 4x6–8; Hollow rocks 4x12–16.
- Day B: Backpack front squat 5x6–8 (3–1–X); Chin-up EMOM 12 min (alt 2 reps + 1 scap pull); Pike push-ups 5x6–8; Single-leg RDL 4x6–8/leg; Side plank with top-leg raise 3x25–35s/side.
- Day C: Push clusters 6 clusters (add 1 rep total vs Week 5); Chin negatives 5x2 at 8–10s + 1–2 assisted singles; Lunges 4x9–10/leg; Hip thrust pump 3x12; Anti-rotation 3x25–30s/side.

Week 7 (Heaviest week)
- Day A: Push-up 7x3–5 (3s down, 1s pause); Chins 10x2 assisted (least help); Bulgarians 6x4–5/leg; Hip thrust 5x5–6 (2s pause); RKC plank 4x15–20s.
- Day B: Backpack front squat 4x8 (2–0–X, last set AMRAP to 1–2 RIR); Pull-up EMOM 10–12 min (2 reps odd, 1 long eccentric even); Pike push-up deficit 4x5–6; Single-leg RDL 3x8/leg (2s bottom pause); Side plank hip taps 3x12–15/side.
- Day C: Contrast push-ups x5 rounds (4 heavy + 6 speed); Chin ladders 1–2–3 x3 ladders + 1 slow eccentric; Split squat 4x8/leg moderate; Hip bridge iso 2x45–60s + 1x20 pumps; Anti-rotation 3x25–30s/side.

Week 8 (Consolidate/mini-test)
- Day A: Push-up top set to 1–2 RIR at hardest leverage; then 3x4 back-offs (~90% diff). Chins: 6–8 single attempts (or top hold + slow eccentric). Bulgarians 4x6/leg; Hip thrust 3x6–8.
- Day B: Backpack front squat 3x8 easy-moderate; Chin density EMOM 8–10 min (2 reps); Pike push-up 4x6–8; Single-leg RDL 3x8/leg; Core choice 3 sets.
- Day C: Push clusters 4 clusters (16–24 total reps); Chin negatives 3x2 (8–10s) + 2x6–8 inverted rows; Lunge 3x8/leg; Hip bridge pump 2x20; Mobility focus 8–10 min.

Phase 3 — Strength Density & Pull-up Chase (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: Convert strength to higher-quality volume, push toward first strict chin-up, maintain leg strength. 3 full-body days; include EMOMs and clusters.

Week 9
- Day A (Push emphasis, pull skill)
  - Decline or pseudo planche-lean push-up 6x5–8
  - Chin-up clusters 10x1–3 assisted/negatives (30–45s rest; aim 15–25 total reps)
  - Pike push-up 3x6–8
  - Inverted row (feet elevated if strong) 3x8–12
  - Hollow to arch rocks 3x12
- Day B (Lower strength)
  - Bulgarian split squat heavy 5x5/leg (backpack)
  - Backpack front squat/Zercher hold squats 4x8–10 (2–3s down)
  - Hip thrust heavy 4x8–10 (2s pause)
  - Single-leg RDL 3x8/leg
  - Backpack front-hold marches 3x30–45s
- Day C (Pull emphasis, push volume)
  - Pull-up EMOM 10 min: odd 2–3 assisted; even 1 long eccentric (6–8s) + 1 scap pull
  - Push-up volume 5x8–12 at challenging leverage (add backpack if floor is easy)
  - Row variation 3x10–12
  - Core: Side plank reach-through 3x10/side + dead bug 3x8/side

Week 10
- Progress: reduce assistance on chins; attempt 1–2 true bodyweight singles if close. Add slight load to push-ups if >12 reps on floor. Add 10–20% backpack load to Bulgarians or 1 extra set. Optionally extend EMOMs by 2 minutes.

Week 11 (Micro-peak)
- Day A: Chin-up singles practice 8–12 attempts with 60–90s rest—strict reps if possible; otherwise top hold + slow eccentric.
- Day B: Bulgarian split squat 6x4/leg heavy; Hip thrust 5x6–8 heavy; Finish with quad/ham isometrics 2x20–30s.
- Day C: Push-up ladder 1-2-3-4-5-4-3-2-1 (30–40s rests) at chosen leverage; Rows 4x6–8; Chins 3x3–4 light assisted to keep pattern. Core each day (hollow/RKC/anti-rotation).

Week 12 (Deload/test)
- Reduce total sets by 30–40%, avoid failure.
- Tests:
  - Chin-up: 3–4 singles attempts; best outcome = strict rep, long top hold, or 12s eccentric.
  - Push-ups: Max quality set (stop 1 shy of failure).
  - Bulgarians: AMRAP at Week 9–10 load (stop 1–2 RIR).
- Light accessories + mobility focus.

Cardio plan (2–3x/week, 15–30 min)
- Intensity: Mostly RPE 4–6; intervals RPE 7–9 used sparingly.
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): 2x/week
  - Session A steady: 15–20 min low-impact mix (marching, toe taps, shadow boxing) at RPE 4–5.
  - Session B intervals: 8 x 30s hard (RPE 7) + 45s easy; 5-min warm-up, short cool-down.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): 2–3x/week
  - Session C tempo steady: 12–16 min at RPE 5–6 (plus warm-up/cool-down).
  - Session D mixed intervals: 6–10 x 40s hard + 40–60s easy.
  - Session E stairs (if available): 10–15 min continuous stair walks RPE 5–6.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): 2–3x/week
  - Session F ladder intervals: 20–40–60–40–20s x 1–2 ladders with equal rest.
  - Session G longer easy: 15–20 min continuous at RPE 4–5.
  - Session H threshold taste: 3–4 x 3 min at RPE 6–7 with 2 min easy.

Saturday finisher (choose one each week, 20–30 min)
- Option 1 EMOM Gauntlet (20 min): blocks of push-ups + shadow boxing; assisted chins/negatives + climbers; split squats; core + brisk march.
- Option 2 Deck of Cards (15–25 min cap): suits map to push-ups, chins/rows (3–6 reps), split squats (per-leg half card), toe-tap/jacks (seconds = 2x card).
- Option 3 Rings/Bar Playground (if rings added): 4–6 rounds, 45s on/15s off: rows, push-ups, split-squat jumps (or calf-raise), core, shadow boxing. Rest 60–90s between rounds.

Mobility routine
- Daily micro (5–8 min): 90/90 hip lift breaths; cat–cow; thoracic openers; hip CARs; ankle rocks; hip flexor stretch; wrist rocks.
- Pre-lift warm-up (10 min): marching/arm swings; world’s greatest stretch; squat pry; hip airplanes; scapular pulls + shoulder circles; ankle rocks; dead bug + plank.
- Post-session (3–5 min): easy breathing + child’s pose with side reach, doorway pec stretch, hip flexor stretch.
- Deep sessions (15–20 min, 1–2x/week):
  - Session A (hips/ankles/low back): 90/90 switches, pigeon or figure-4, Cossack with support, knee-to-wall ankles, decompression hang.
  - Session B (shoulders/T-spine/wrists): towel-roll T-spine extension, thread-the-needle, doorway pec stretch, lat opener on chair, wall slides, prone Y-T-W, wrist sequence.

Nutrition summary
- Calories: Start at maintenance to slight surplus (+150–250 kcal/day). On training days, bias carbs higher; rest days at maintenance or −0 to −150 kcal if aiming recomposition.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (30–40 g per meal across 3–4 meals).
- Carbs: Pre-workout 30–60 g + protein 20–35 g 60–120 min before; post-workout 25–40 g protein + 40–80 g carbs within 2 hours.
- Fats: 0.7–1.0 g/kg/day, mostly unsaturated.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day; fruits/veg 4–6 servings/day; legumes 3–4x/week.
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day + ~500 ml around training.
- Supplements (optional): Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day; vitamin D3 per local guidance if low sun; omega-3 if not eating fish (consult a professional).
- Weekly habits progression: establish protein and plate method (Weeks 1–2), fiber/consistency (Weeks 3–4), caloric tweaks via weight trends (Weeks 5–6), micronutrients/sleep (Weeks 7–8), performance fueling (Weeks 9–10), keep meals familiar in test week (Weeks 11–12).

Weekly layout example
- Mon: Strength (Phase plan) + pre-lift warm-up + optional 3–5 min cool-down.
- Tue: Cardio (steady or intervals) + Daily micro-mobility + optional Deep Session A.
- Wed: Strength + warm-up.
- Thu: Off or cardio (easy) + Deep Session B mobility.
- Fri: Strength + warm-up.
- Sat: Finisher Day (pick option) + light mobility.
- Sun: Rest, walk, or gentle mobility only.

Progress tracking and targets
- Log sets/reps, leverage/assistance, RPE, and notes.
- Aim by Week 12:
  - 1 strict chin-up (or 12s controlled eccentric and strong assisted doubles).
  - Push-ups: 20+ strict floor reps or 6–10 strong reps at decline/backpack.
  - Bulgarians: solid 5–6 rep sets/leg with front load.
- If two consecutive sessions underperform, reduce volume by ~30% for a week (mini-deload), then resume.

Equipment roadmap (space-friendly)
- Near-term: resistance bands with door anchor; adjustable dumbbells (to ~20 kg/hand) or one heavy kettlebell (16–24 kg); rings/TRX for variety.
- Later: loadable DB handles + small plates, foldable bench, sandbag, dip belt/strap for weighted pull-ups.
